summary: The base synchronously blocks the ASGI event loop during slow Prometheus collection. The exact candidate moves collection to a bounded child process, fails overlapping scrapes fast, and fixes the independently reproduced repeated Accept and Accept-Encoding regressions. No remaining source-level counterexample was found.

tests.what_was_measured: A 0.35-second synchronous collector caused 0.331 seconds of event-loop timer lag while /metrics returned 200.
Reproduced both prior-review counterexamples: duplicate Accept failed OpenMetrics selection and duplicate Accept-Encoding failed gzip selection.
Five candidate regression tests covering real exposition, singleflight, timeout, failure, and cancellation passed.
Repeated Accept and Accept-Encoding behavior matched prometheus_client.make_asgi_app.
A slow mocked child returned 200, an overlapping scrape returned 503, and event-loop lag was 0.001 seconds.
Independent weighted/repeated negotiation cases and slash routing matched the Prometheus reference.

gpu_execution.evidence: The reviewed contract is CPU-side ASGI and Prometheus process isolation; the available ROCm/gfx950 GPU cannot reproduce the reported eight-H100 PD topology and was not used.

remaining_limitations: The original eight-H100 multi-node single-tokenizer PD deployment and decode-side connection-loss logs were unavailable.
No model weights or sustained production scrape workload were used; deterministic ASGI-level reproduction establishes the blocking mechanism and isolation behavior.
The prepared host is ROCm 7.2/gfx950 rather than CUDA 13/H100.
No native source changed and repository-environment.json declares no native build target, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
